titleEn: Renovation Warranty in Vancouver and BC: What Is Covered and How to Use It
titleZh: 溫哥華及卑詩省裝修保固指南：保固範圍與索賠流程（2026）
contentEn:
When a renovation goes wrong, the warranty is your first line of protection. In British Columbia, the Homeowner Protection Act establishes mandatory warranty coverage for all residential renovation work performed by licensed contractors. Reno Stars, a Vancouver renovation company serving the Lower Mainland, operates under these protections and helps clients understand exactly what their warranty covers — and how to make a claim if something breaks down.

What BC Law Requires: The 2-5-10 Warranty Framework

BC's mandatory warranty system under the Homeowner Protection Act (RSBC 1996, c. 367) covers every renovation performed by a licensed residential builder. The protection is tiered by defect type:

  • Two-year warranty: Covers defects in labour and materials for two years from the date of completion. This is the most common coverage dispute for finished renovations — it catches things like faulty plumbing fixtures, improper electrical connections, and flooring that delaminates within the warranty window.
  • Five-year warranty: Covers the building envelope — walls, windows, doors, and the systems that keep weather out. Water intrusion through a window frame installed incorrectly, or a roof that fails before year five, both fall here.
  • Ten-year warranty: Covers structural defects. If load-bearing elements of the renovation fail — a support beam installed incorrectly, foundation issues that worsen over time — the ten-year window applies.

This warranty is backed by BC Housing (the Crown corporation regulating residential builders in BC), not by the contractor alone. Even if a contractor goes out of business, coverage through the BC Housing warranty program remains in effect for the stated periods.

Planning a renovation in Vancouver or the Lower Mainland? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars for your kitchen, bathroom, or whole-home renovation.

What Is and Is Not Covered

BC Housing's warranty guidelines make clear distinctions that many homeowners discover only when filing a claim.

  • Covered: Defective workmanship or materials supplied by the contractor. A faucet that leaks because of a faulty cartridge, not because of user damage, is covered. Cabinets that warp due to improper installation are covered.
  • Not covered: Damage caused by the homeowner's misuse, neglect, or failure to maintain the property. Modifications made by the homeowner after completion are also excluded — adding a bidet to a toilet after the plumber leaves, for example, voids the plumbing warranty for that fixture.
  • Not covered: Normal wear and tear. Hardwood floors scuffed from daily use, grout that needs re-sealing after several years, and weather-related minor cracking in concrete driveways are maintenance items, not warranty claims.
  • Not covered: Work performed by subcontractors hired independently by the homeowner. Any contractor a homeowner hires directly — without going through the licensed builder — falls outside the warranty entirely.

Appliances and fixtures installed as part of a renovation carry manufacturer warranties separate from the construction warranty. A dishwasher that fails in year three is a manufacturer claim; the plumbing connections to it are the contractor's warranty.

How to File a Warranty Claim in BC

The process for a BC renovation warranty claim has defined steps. Knowing them before a problem occurs saves time and frustration.

Step 1 — Document the defect in writing. Take photographs with timestamps, note the date of discovery, and describe the problem in plain language. This contemporaneous record becomes critical evidence if the claim is disputed.

Step 2 — Contact the contractor in writing. Email or registered mail gives you proof of delivery. Describe the defect, reference the completion date, and request remedy under warranty. Licensed contractors in BC are required to respond to warranty claims within a reasonable time.

Step 3 — Contact BC Housing if the contractor does not respond or denies the claim. BC Housing's consumer protection team handles warranty disputes for licensed builders. They can investigate, mediate, and in some cases escalate to arbitration.

Step 4 — Use the BC Civil Resolution Tribunal (CRT) for claims under $5,000. The CRT handles renovation disputes efficiently and at low cost compared to going to court. For amounts above $5,000, the Supreme Court of BC is the venue, which makes early negotiation more attractive.

How Reno Stars Handles Warranty on Vancouver Projects

Reno Stars provides warranties on its renovation work in Vancouver and across the Lower Mainland, and maintains a written warranty document with every project. Lisa Jung, a Vancouver client who completed a whole-home renovation with Reno Stars, described the experience: "This is our second project with Reno Stars, and once again the experience was excellent. Sylvia, Ryan, and Jasper make a fantastic team, the workmanship was great, everything stayed on budget, and communication was always quick and easy."

For clients in Vancouver, North Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and Coquitlam, Reno Stars provides a project-specific warranty document that clearly states what is covered, for how long, and how to initiate service. Contact the Reno Stars team through the Vancouver office for warranty service requests.

Renovation Contract Clauses That Affect Your Warranty Rights

Before signing a renovation contract in BC, review how the contract addresses warranty. Several clauses can limit or extend your protections beyond the statutory minimum:

  • Warranty duration clauses: Many contractors offer an extended one-year labour warranty on top of the two-year statutory minimum. A "five-year warranty on labour" from the contractor is separate from and in addition to the five-year building envelope warranty required by law.
  • Limitation of liability clauses: Some contracts cap the contractor's maximum liability to the contract value. BC courts have found certain limitation clauses unconscionable, particularly where the defect causes damage beyond the contract price — but this is not guaranteed.
  • Dispute resolution clauses: Mandatory arbitration clauses in renovation contracts are enforceable in BC, but the CRT process remains available regardless of what a contract says, because it is a statutory right under the Homeowner Protection Act.

Warranty Disputes We See Most Often in Vancouver Renovations

Based on Reno Stars' experience with Vancouver renovation projects, the following areas generate the most warranty enquiries:

  • Tile and grout: Efflorescence (white mineral deposits on tile), grout cracking in shower enclosures, and tile lippage (uneven tile surfaces) are common. Grout cracking within six months of installation is typically a workmanship issue covered under warranty; cracking that appears after two years is usually maintenance.
  • Cabinet hardware: Door hinges that stop staying closed, drawer slides that fail, and soft-close mechanisms that stop functioning are frequently reported. Functional hardware failures within two years of installation are generally covered.
  • Plumbing: Slow leaks at connection points, cartridges that fail, and water heater issues are covered when caused by installation defects rather than water quality or pressure issues.
  • Windows and doors: Condensation between double-glazed panes (seal failure), doors that no longer close properly, and window hardware failures fall under the five-year building envelope warranty when caused by installation.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the BC renovation warranty apply to all contractors?

Only licensed residential builders are required to provide the 2-5-10 warranty. Homeowners hiring an unlicensed contractor for renovation work in BC are not covered by the statutory warranty and have limited recourse if something goes wrong. Always verify a contractor's licence at the BC Housing website before signing a contract.

How long do I have to file a warranty claim in BC?

The warranty periods run from the date of completion of the renovation. Claims for two-year labour and material defects must be filed within the two-year window. Structural defect claims (ten-year) must be filed within ten years of completion. BC Housing recommends filing as soon as a defect is discovered rather than waiting until near the deadline, because collecting evidence and scheduling inspections takes time.

Can a contractor charge for warranty work?

If the issue is a legitimate defect covered by the warranty, the contractor cannot charge for the repair. However, if an inspection reveals the issue was caused by homeowner misuse, neglect, or an unauthorized modification, the contractor may charge for the service call and repair. Always get a written explanation of charges before authorizing work.

What if the contractor refuses to honour the warranty?

Contact BC Housing's consumer protection division to open a dispute. BC Housing can appoint an independent inspector, mediate between the parties, and in some cases order remediation. For disputes involving amounts under $5,000, homeowners can file directly with the BC Civil Resolution Tribunal at a fraction of the cost of going to court.

Does home insurance cover renovation defects?

Home insurance covers sudden and accidental damage — for example, a pipe that bursts and causes water damage. It does not cover gradual deterioration, defective workmanship, or materials that fail over time. The contractor's warranty is the correct recourse for construction defects, not your home insurance policy.
contentZh:
裝修工程出了問題時，保固服務是屋主的第一道防線。卑詩省的《屋主保障法》（Homeowner Protection Act）規定，持有牌照的住宅建築商進行的所有裝修工程都必須提供強制保固。溫哥華裝修公司聚星裝修（Reno Stars）在大溫哥華地區提供服務，保固範圍完全符合省府規定，並協助客戶了解保固的具體內容以及如何申請理賠。

卑詩省法律規定：2-5-10 保固框架

根據《屋主保障法》（RSBC 1996，第367章），持牌住宅建築商的每項裝修工程均受強制保固保障，按缺陷類型分為三個層級：

  • 兩年保固：涵蓋完工之日起兩年內的工藝及材料瑕疵。常見案例包括：水龍頭因軸芯問題而漏水（非人為損壞）、因安裝不當導致地板分層、浴室瓷磚脫落等。
  • 五年保固：涵蓋建築外殼，包括牆壁、門窗及防水系統。窗框安裝不當導致滲水，或屋頂在五年內失效，均屬此範圍。
  • 十年保固：涵蓋結構性缺陷，包括支撐樑柱安裝錯誤或地基問題逐漸惡化等情況。

此項保固由卑詩省房屋局（BC Housing）提供保障，並非僅由承辦商負責。即使承辦商倒閉，保固仍按各期限規定持續有效。

保固範圍：涵蓋與不涵蓋的事項

卑詩省房屋局的保固指引明確區分以下項目：

  • 涵蓋：承辦商工藝或材料瑕疵導致的問題。例如水龍頭軸芯故障（非人為損壞）、櫥櫃因安裝不當而變形。
  • 不涵蓋：因屋主使用不當、疏忽或未妥善保養導致的損壞。完工後屋主自行進行的修改（如自行加裝免治馬桶）亦不在保固範圍內。
  • 不涵蓋：正常損耗。地板日常使用刮痕、瓷磚填縫劑數年後需重新密封、混凝土車道因天氣而出現輕微裂縫等，均屬保養項目，非保固索賠範圍。
  • 不涵蓋：屋主未透過持牌建築商聘用的分包商工程。屋主直接僱用的任何施工人員均不受保固保障。

如何在卑詩省申請裝修保固

卑詩省裝修保固索賠有明確程序，提前了解可節省時間與麻煩：

步驟一：以書面記錄缺陷。拍下帶時間標記的照片，記錄發現日期，並以通俗語言描述問題。此記錄在爭議時將成為重要證據。

步驟二：以書面聯繫承辦商。使用電子郵件或掛號信件，並保留送達證明。說明缺陷、引用完工日期，並要求按保固進行維修。

步驟三：若承辦商不回應或拒絕索賠，聯繫卑詩省房屋局。房屋局的消費者保障團隊負責處理持牌建築商的保固爭議，可進行調查、調解，並在必要時升級至仲裁程序。

步驟四：對於5,000加元以下的索賠，使用卑詩省民事調解法庭（CRT）。相較於法院訴訟，CRT處理裝修爭議的效率更高且費用更低。超過5,000加元的索賠則需向卑詩省最高法院提出訴訟。

聚星裝修如何處理溫哥華項目的保固

聚星裝修為溫哥華及大溫哥華地區的項目提供書面保固文件，清楚說明涵蓋範圍、期限及申請服務流程。在溫哥華完成整屋裝修的 Lisa Jung 评价道：「這是我們第二次與聚星裝修合作，體驗一如既往地出色。Sylvia、Ryan 和 Jasper 組成很棒的團隊，工藝精湛，預算控制得當，溝通始終迅速順暢。」

如需申請保固服務，請聯繫聚星裝修溫哥華辦事處。

影響保固權利的裝修合約條款

在卑詩省簽署裝修合約前，請留意以下可能影響您保障權益的條款：

  • 保固期限條款：許多承辦商提供較法定最低兩年更長的書面人工保固（如五年人工保固），此為法定保固的補充，而非替代。
  • 責任上限條款：部分合約將承辦商最高責任限於合約金額。卑詩省法院已裁定，在缺陷造成超出合約價格的損失時，此類條款可能不予執行。
  • 爭議解決條款：強制仲裁條款在卑詩省可強制執行，但根據《屋主保障法》的法定權利，CRT程序不受合約條款約束。

溫哥華裝修常見保固爭議

根據聚星裝修的經驗，以下項目最常收到保固查詢：瓷磚及填縫劑（六個月內填縫劑開裂通常屬保固範圍）、櫥櫃鉸鏈及滑軌故障、管道連接點滲漏，以及門窗硬體問題。

常見問題

卑詩省的裝修保固是否適用於所有承辦商？

僅持牌住宅建築商須提供2-5-10保固。聘請無牌承辦商進行裝修的屋主不受法定保固保障出了問題時追索權有限。請在簽約前於卑詩省房屋局網站查核承辦商牌照。

我有多長時間提出保固索賠？

各層級保固期限從裝修完工日起算。兩年工藝及材料瑕疵索賠須在兩年期限內提出；結構缺陷（十年）索賠則須在完工後十年內提出。卑詩省房屋局建議一旦發現缺陷便立即提出申請，而非等到期限將屆之際。

承辦商是否可以就保固工作收費？

若問題屬於保固涵蓋的合法缺陷，承辦商不得收取維修費用。然而，若檢驗後確認問題由屋主使用不當或未經授權的修改所導致，承辦商有權就服務及維修收費。請在授權施工前取得書面費用說明。

若承辦商拒絕履行保固怎么辦？

聯繫卑詩省房屋局消費者保障部門提出爭議。房屋局可指派獨立檢驗員、調解雙方，並在部分情況下下令補救。對於5,000加元以下的索賠，屋主可直接向卑詩省民事調解法庭（CRT）提交申請，費用遠低於法院訴訟。

房屋保險是否涵蓋裝修缺陷？

房屋保險僅涵蓋突發及意外事故導致的損壞，例如爆管造成的水浸損失。保險不涵蓋漸進性損耗、缺陷工藝或隨時間失效的材料。裝修缺陷的正確追索途徑是承辦商的保固，而非房屋保險。
